Merged v332: absorbed DIN 1337 (DBAASP:6276; PMID:21321136) -- same molecule held under two source schemes. The rows differ at positions 9 and 12: four dehydrophenylalanine here against two on the absorbed row, which has ordinary Phe at those positions. Table 1 of the shared paper (PMID:21321136, PMC3088198) lists VSL3 with a dPhe count of 4 and prints its sequence with four dF and no ordinary Phe, at Length 14 and Charge +5 -- matching this row residue for residue. DBAASP:6276's sequence is a partial transcription, spelling the same residue two ways within one sequence, and was not carried over. See changesets/master_v332.json. Sequence CONFIRMED against Table 1 of the shared reference, PMID:21321136 = DOI 10.1128/AAC.01493-10 (Pathak & Chauhan, Antimicrob Agents Chemother 2011;55:2178-88, open access PMC3088198), supplied by the curator as an image on 2026-10-01 and transcribed in full in changesets/master_v332.json. The table has a dedicated dPhe-count column; VSL3's reads 4, its printed sequence is Ac-K-A-dF-K-A-dF-W-K-dF-V-K-dF-V-K-NH2 with no ordinary Phe, and its Length (14) and Charge (+5) match this row. The table also confirms this row's existing note that VSL3 is VS1 extended at the N-terminus by Lys-Ala-dPhe. DBAASP:6276 recorded only two dPhe, converting positions 9 and 12 to ordinary Phe, and its sequence was not carried over when DIN 1337 was merged in. NOTED, NOT ACTED ON: the table gives VSL3's observed MW as 1,808.2 against 1,803.7 calculated, a +4.5 Da gap and the largest of the eight peptides listed; two dPhe-to-Phe substitutions would account for about +4 Da, which may be how DBAASP's reading arose, but the paper's own count column and sequence both say four.

Annotation: Merged v333: absorbed DIN 1281 (DBAASP:5742; PMID:24317473) -- same molecule held under two source schemes. This row's position 8 was first corrected from `(d-Ile)` to `(d-allo-Ile)`, the published structure being K-I-I-(d-Phe)-(d-Leu)-I-(d-Ala)-(d-allo-Ile) (PMID:24317473, curator's reading 2026-10-01); it was otherwise correct in ring direction, starting residue and every other residue. The tokens still differ from the absorbed row because DBAASP:5742 writes the same ring in the REVERSE direction: read backwards from its D-Ala it reproduces the published order exactly, residue for residue. Its residues and configurations are all correct; only the direction is wrong, and the reversed form is not carried over. See changesets/master_v333.json. Position 8 corrected v333 from `(d-Ile)` to `(d-allo-Ile)`, diastereomers differing at the beta carbon, against the structure published in PMID:24317473 = DOI 10.3390/md11124834 (Pesic et al., Mar Drugs 2013;11:4834-57, open access PMC3877890), read by the curator 2026-10-01: K-I-I-(d-Phe)-(d-Leu)-I-(d-Ala)-(d-allo-Ile). That was this row's only error; its ring direction, starting residue and all other residues already matched. The absorbed row DIN 1281 (DBAASP:5742) had every residue and configuration right, including the allo-Ile this row lacked, but wrote the ring in the REVERSE DIRECTION -- read backwards from its D-Ala it reproduces the published order exactly. Because a cyclic peptide's ring is directional (each carbonyl bonds to the next residue's nitrogen), a reversed ring describes the retro isomer, a different molecule, and not merely a different starting point as in the rotation cases at v324, v325 and v327; DBAASP's string is read as a notation artefact rather than a claim about retro-champacyclin, since the two records share one paper, one name, one composition and every configuration. The reversed form was not carried over. Spectrum left as `Gram-negative` rather than taking DIN 1281's `Broad-spectrum`: seven of that row's eight MIC entries were empty `-=NA` placeholders and its only real measurement is 40% Inhibition = 25 uM against Pectobacterium carotovorum, a Gram-negative. Those seven are dropped as malformed by the merge and their organisms do not reach `Tested Against` -- the open part of register item mic-5, for which DBAASP holds no recoverable note.

NO MIC VALUE EXISTS FOR ANY ORGANISM IN THIS PAPER, and none should be added without a new source. PMID:24692199 (Niggemann et al., Chembiochem 2014;15:1021-9) states its method as "Cyclopeptide 1 (20 microg) was tested on paper disc (6 mm diameter) in agar diffusion assays against the following strains" - a single-loading zone-of-inhibition assay, which does not yield a minimum inhibitory concentration. The twelve strains it names are all recorded in Tested Against: Escherichia coli TolC, Klebsiella pneumoniae (the paper prints "Klebsiella pneumonia"), Pseudomonas aeruginosa, Staphylococcus aureus, Micrococcus luteus, Mycobacterium phlei, Candida albicans, Hansenula anomala, Saccharomyces cerevisiae, Aspergillus niger, Botrytis cinerea and Pythium debaryanum. THE ONLY ANTIMICROBIAL RESULT THE PAPER REPORTS is qualitative and concerns one organism: baceridin "showed weak antimicrobial activity against Staphylococcus aureus in agar diffusion assays". Nothing is stated for the other eleven - neither activity nor inactivity - so nothing is recorded for them. TWO OF THOSE TWELVE WERE MISSING FROM BOTH ROWS before this merge, Staphylococcus aureus and Hansenula anomala, and S. aureus is the one organism with a reported result; E. coli was held without its TolC strain designation. TEN `-=NA` PLACEHOLDERS WERE REMOVED at the dup-202 merge (register item mic-5). They were not recoverable values: DBAASP's notes for all ten are empty on card 5374, and the paper never measured an MIC. This differs from the mic-5 cases repaired at v336 from a heat map, and from the M. bovis BCG placeholders dropped at v335 where a number existed but was untabulated. CYTOTOXICITY: `IC50=2 ug/ml (L929 mouse fibroblast)` is added from the paper's text - "baceridin (1) exhibited moderate cytotoxic activity (IC50 = 2 microg mL-1) in assays with a L929 mouse fibroblast cell line" - an organism absent from both rows. The four values against human cancer lines (HCT 116, HCT 116-/-p53, RKO, HeLa, 1-2 ug/ml) come from elsewhere in the paper, are carried unchanged, and are NOT verified against it. NOTE ON THIS ROW'S SHAPE: Tested Against is deliberately a SUPERSET of the organisms MIC measures - seventeen named, five measured - because twelve were tested with no quantitative result. That is the data model question register item mic-5 has been deferring since v324, and this row is the first concrete case of it. ACTIVITY is left as `active` and not revised, although the paper's own word for the antimicrobial effect is "weak" and its only quantified activity is cytotoxic; Spectrum keeps `Gram-positive`, which the evidence supports.
Annotation: Merged v343: absorbed DIN 1206 (DBAASP:5374; PMID:24692199) -- same molecule held under two source schemes. DIN 1206 (DBAASP:5374) absorbed as the same molecule, register item dup-202. The two rows had differed in TWO ways at once: the ring was written in opposite directions, and one stereocentre disagreed (d-Ile against d-allo-Ile). Both are settled from PMID:24692199, read by the curator 2026-10-08. The abstract gives the ring as W-(d-Ala)-(d-allo-Ile)-V-(d-Leu)-L written C TO N; reversed to N-to-C and rotated to Trp that is W-L-(d-Leu)-V-(d-allo-Ile)-(d-Ala), which is DBAASP's ring. APD6 appears to have transcribed the abstract's C-to-N string into a field read N-to-C, inverting the ring, and to have written d-Ile for d-allo-Ile. The retained row's Sequence is corrected to the curator's preferred N-to-C rendering before this merge; allow_token_mismatch is passed because the absorbed row's string starts at a different residue of the same ring and was deliberately not normalised, so the rotation stays visible. The absorbed row's TEN `-=NA` placeholders were removed first and no value invented: the paper's antimicrobial work is agar diffusion at a single 20 microg loading, which yields no MIC, and DBAASP's notes for all ten are empty. The twelve organisms the paper tested are recorded in Tested Against on the retained row - including Staphylococcus aureus and Hansenula anomala, which were absent from both rows, and E. coli TolC with its strain - so the panel survives the merge rather than being deleted with the placeholders.See changesets/master_v343.json.

READ THIS AS AN INFERENCE, NOT A DETERMINATION: the paper says of the two Lys residues at positions 7 and 10 that they "displayed either a D- or L-configuration, which could not be distinguished from each other", adding that this is "consistent with the prediction from antiSMASH where epimerization domains were predicted at the 3rd, 7th, and 11th modules". The Streptococcus panels were run in CAMHB with 3% horse blood. The five [MHB] entries (Bacillus subtilis ATCC 6051; Staphylococcus epidermidis ATCC 14990; Staphylococcus aureus ATCC 29213; Staphylococcus aureus ATCC 700698, MRSA; Escherichia coli ATCC 10798) are from PMID:39178334 (DBAASP's reference 2); the other 50 DBAASP entries attribute to its reference 1, the bioRxiv preprint of PMID:37611581. MERGE (v334) -- absorbed DIN 5992 (DBAASP:24160); 15 shared measurement(s) kept once (retained wording kept, absorbed medium tag added where missing), 6 added from DIN 5992; no value altered or converted, and none dropped. MIC consolidated at the dup-215 merge (DIN 5992 absorbed). The row now holds twenty-one verified per-organism values from PMID:29987155: the fifteen Table 1 reference strains, and six carbapenem-resistant strains from Table 3 (E. coli ATCC BAA-2469 2, ATCC BAA-2471 4; K. pneumoniae ATCC BAA-2146 0.5, NCTC 13443 1, NCTC 13439 1, NCTC 13442 1 ug/ml). All four tables of the paper are transcribed and curator-confirmed in the evidence store as PMID_29987155_table1 to _table4; consult those rather than re-reading the paper. NOT CARRIED INTO MIC, and recorded here instead: Table 2's clinical-isolate panels (C. freundii n=16, 1-4; E. cloacae n=13, 1-4; E. coli n=101, 2-32; ciprofloxacin-resistant E. coli n=19, 2-32; gentamicin-resistant E. coli n=6, 4; polymyxin-B-resistant E. coli n=2, 4-8; K. pneumoniae n=56, 0.5-16; ciprofloxacin-resistant K. pneumoniae n=27, 0.5-16; gentamicin-resistant K. pneumoniae n=16, 0.5-2, all ug/ml, with MIC50/MIC90 in the transcript); Table 3's remaining eighteen carbapenem-resistant strains; Table 4's colistin-resistant panels (E. coli n=25, 1-4; K. pneumoniae n=46, 0.25-128, by resistance mechanism). These are panel statistics, not per-organism MICs, and the (organism) slot cannot carry their populations. Also not carried: DBAASP's HepG2 entry, stored as the malformed placeholder `=NA ug/ml`, whose DBAASP note reads "Not active up to 256 micro M" - a cytotoxicity result, not an MIC. FOUR DBAASP VALUES WERE REJECTED as wrong against the paper: `4-8 (E. coli)` is the 2 polymyxin-B-resistant isolates, not the n=101 panel (2-32); `0.5-2 (K. pneumoniae)` is the 16 gentamicin-resistant isolates, not the n=56 panel (0.5-16); `1 (E. cloacae, "3 carbapenem resistant strains")` understates five strains spanning 1-2; and `0.25-2 (K. pneumoniae, "colistin-resistant 41 strains")` is a 46-strain panel spanning 0.25-128, a 64-fold understatement. ORGANISM NAMES: the paper prints "Citrobacter kozeri" (its own typo for C. koseri) and "Enterobacter aerogenes"; both are recorded here under their current valid names, C. koseri DSM 4595 and Klebsiella aerogenes DSM 30053, matching DBAASP and the master's majority usage. The paper's spelling is preserved verbatim in the Table 1 transcript. MEDIUM: the `[MHB]` tag now on every entry comes from DBAASP card 24160, applied across the row by the merge; it was not read from the paper, whose Methods were not transcribed for this ruling.

Both rows cite PMID:29987155 and their fifteen Table 1 reference-strain MICs are identical; compare_evidence scores them 15/15 and 14/15 against the stored transcript evidence/PMID_29987155_table1, with the column-shift check clean. The absorbed row's `d-Orn` at position 5 is correct against the paper and has been applied to the retained sequence; its `2-F-PHE*` is DBAASP's unmapped raw token for the residue AMPUDB codes `oFPhe` (2-fluorophenylalanine, CID 9465), so the retained code stands and allow_token_mismatch covers that textual difference. The absorbed row brings six carbapenem-resistant strain MICs verified against evidence/PMID_29987155_table3. Eight of its entries were removed before the merge: four DBAASP roll-ups that disagree with the paper, three that are correct but are panel statistics rather than per-organism MICs, and one malformed HepG2 placeholder - see the changeset rationale and MIC Notes.See changesets/master_v334.json.

Annotation: Merged v324: absorbed DIN 1183 (DBAASP:5297; PMID:12712499) -- same molecule held under two source schemes. The two DBAASP records write the same head-to-tail ring from different starting residues (yPVKyPKL and VKyPKLyP, a rotation by 2); their cards carry byte-identical SMILES, the same 1->8 NCB amide bond and the same name. See changesets/master_v324.json. The twelve absorbed MIC entries were stored as `-=NA` placeholders; dbaasp_activities shows each carries DBAASP's note "Not active up to 150 micro g/ml" (LBB, 5E5 CFU, PMID:12712499), so they were rewritten to the house censored form `MIC=>150 ug/ml` before the merge rather than being dropped as malformed -- a real negative result, and the twelve organisms it covers, would otherwise have been lost. Activity set to `inactive` on that evidence. Spectrum deliberately left blank rather than taking DIN 1183's `Broad-spectrum`, which its own twelve results contradict: a compound inactive against everything tested has no spectrum to state. Sequence rewritten from `(d-Tyr)PVK(d-Tyr)PKL` to `VK(d-Tyr)PKL(d-Tyr)P` -- the same ring from a different start -- so that GS8 matches the valine-start writing used by every other member of its family in the master (DIN 27 gramicidin S; DINs 678, 683, 689 GS14 analogues). Length and Charge are unaffected.

This row is compound 12 of PMID:25495219 Table 2, which is battacin (compound 10 of the same table, our DIN 1934) bearing Fmoc at the N-terminus in place of the 3-hydroxy-6-methyloctanoyl tail; the rest of the peptide is identical. DBAASP:8745 records the parent's tail `3-OH-6-Me-C8` AND the parent's SMILES, both inherited in error, which is why this row and DIN 1934 looked like one molecule -- they are not, and review item 229 is closed as confirmed distinct rather than merged. The MIC panels of the two rows are the paper's own adjacent rows for compounds 10 and 12 and were each verified against it. NOTE for any future structure work: DBAASP:8745's SMILES is battacin's and must not be used for this compound.

All 23 values this row shares with that panel agree with it exactly. Four changes made while the figure was in hand, none of them a value correction. (1) TWO `-=NA` PLACEHOLDERS REPAIRED, not dropped (register item mic-5): Neisseria mucosa ATCC 25996 and Salmonella enterica subsp. enterica are grey "Inactive" cells and are recorded as MIC=>128 ug/ml, the value the paper uses for inactive (curator ruling 2026-10-01). Ref also reduced from `10.1038/nchembio.2207; PMID:27748750` to the PMID alone, the two having been one paper in two notations. Identical reported values throughout (E. coli 16, K. pneumoniae 4 ug/ml, IC50 0.36 +/- 0.08), ruled one compound by the curator 2026-10-08. DBAASP:24181 (synthetic) vs DBAASP:24162 (nonribosomal); RDKit C50H91N21O13 vs C54H101N23O12, a difference of putrescine minus water, with different InChIKey skeletons. Both DBAASP records are named "Odilorhabdin NOSO-95C"; only 5994 is. Removing Dbt costs two-fold against E. coli ATCC 25922 (16 vs 8 ug/ml) and nothing against K. pneumoniae ATCC 43816 (4 vs 4).
